newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus opposition leader fined $800 for protest.
newsitem.headline: Belarus opposition leader fined $800 for protest.

text.p: A Belarus court fined a prominent opposition leader about $800 on Thursday for helping to organise a rally banned by hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.

"This is a political trial. The authorities are dealing with me because I signed the constitution trampled on by the president," Mecheslav Grib, who once headed parliament in the former Soviet republic, told reporters after the ruling.
Grib was one of several leading opposition figures to lead a rally by about 10,000 people on March 15, Constitution Day in the country of 10 million on Russia's western border.
The court fined him 20 million Belarussian roubles ($829) -- the maximum fine for such an offence -- over his role in the protest against a new constitution written by Lukashenko.
Lukashenko, facing a "political spring" by opponents of his increasingly authoritarian rule, has ordered strict controls on political meetings and the display of nationalist symbols.
Grib hoped to be immune to prosecution as his term has not expired as a deputy of the parliament which was disbanded under Lukashenko's constitution, approved at a referendum in November.
But the prosecutor general, Oleg Bozhylko, met Lukashenko late on Wednesday and agreed to lift Grib's immunity.
An official at Bozhylko's office who asked not to be named said the immunity law could be "interpreted in different ways".
The case against a second leading opposition figure, Vasily Novikov, who also attended the court over his role in organising the protest, was postponed until Monday.
The U.S. embassy recently accused Belarus of failing to preserve democracy and human rights and said it was telling investors to put money into neighbouring countries instead.
